## 2. GAPS

Each gap below is written to be handed to Engineer as a standalone,
parallel-buildable ask — no gap depends on another shipping first.

### G1 — Tool durability is not in `/status`

**What exists:** `summarizeInventory()` (`runner.js` ~1886) returns only
`{name, count}` per stack. mineflayer/prismarine-item items already
expose `.durabilityUsed` and `.maxDurability` natively on any stack that
supports it (confirmed against `node_modules/prismarine-item`) — tools,
weapons, and armor; food/blocks/materials simply don't have the property
(`maxDurability` is `undefined`).

**Ask:** extend `summarizeInventory()` to include a `durability` object
only when `it.maxDurability` is truthy:

```js
function summarizeInventory(b) {
  const map = new Map();
  for (const it of b.inventory.items()) {
    const key = it.name;
    const existing = map.get(key);
    const entry = existing || { name: key, count: 0 };
    entry.count += it.count;
    // Durability doesn't sum across a stack sensibly (each tool wears
    // independently) — surface the FIRST/current instance's wear, which
    // is what a driver holding one pickaxe actually cares about. Tools
    // don't stack past 1 in vanilla anyway, so this is exact in practice.
    if (it.maxDurability && entry.durability === undefined) {
      entry.durability = { used: it.durabilityUsed ?? 0, max: it.maxDurability };
    }
    map.set(key, entry);
  }
  return Array.from(map.values());
}
```

Resulting item shape becomes `{name, count}` (unchanged for non-durable
items) or `{name, count, durability:{used,max}}` (tools/armor/weapons).
Backward compatible — `panel.mjs`'s existing inventory-chip rendering
(bot cards, vault) doesn't read `durability` and won't break; Mission
Control reads it when present, omits the field from its tool line when
absent (matches every other "hide chip when null" rule already in this
codebase).

**Owner:** Engineer (`runner.js`). **Size:** ~10 line diff, one function.

### G2 — No durable "mission" / completed-task history

**What exists:** the events ring (`/events`) has task start/done lines
but is in-memory, capped at 500, resets on runner restart — not a record,
a recent-activity window. Nothing else in the codebase tracks completed
tasks at all; grepping "mission" across `runner.js`/`overseer.mjs`/
`DRIVER_GUIDE.md`/`CIV.md` returns zero hits as a formal concept (only
loose FEEDBACK.md prose like "mid-mission").

**This blocks TWO of chief's named fields**: Mission Control's "mission
history" and the Tribe Stat Wall's "missions today." Neither can be built
honestly without this.

**Ask:** a new durable primitive, deliberately mirroring the ledger's own
successful pattern (commit 66a9ca8) exactly — same directory-per-concern
convention, same append-only JSONL, same single-choke-point hook:

- `cave/missions/<bot>.jsonl` (new dir, `.gitignore`d like
  `logs/`/`pids/`/`deaths/`/`ledger/`).
- Hook: `markTaskFinished(task)` (`runner.js` ~656) is already the single
  place every task — however it started, however it ends — gets its
  `finishedAt` stamped. Append one line there:
  ```js
  function markTaskFinished(task) {
    task.finishedAt = new Date().toISOString();
    idleSince = Date.now();
    appendMissionLine(task); // NEW
  }
  ```
- Line shape: `{ ts, bot: name, kind: task.kind, source: task.source, state: task.state, durationMs, detail: task.detail, error: task.result?.error ?? null }`.
  `durationMs` needs the task's start timestamp — `startTask()` (~941)
  already creates the task object; stamp a `startedAt` field on it there
  (one field, same object, no extra state) so `markTaskFinished` can
  subtract.
- **Exclude `idle-guard` and `panic-response` kinds from the mission
  count** (not real driver-requested work) but still log them for
  completeness with a flag, e.g. `{"...", "counts": false}` — mirrors how
  the panel already treats `idle-guard` as "idle," not "working," in
  every other view. "Missions today" = count of lines with
  `counts !== false` and `ts` within the current UTC day, across all bot
  files.
- Same tolerance rules as the ledger: append failure = one `logLine('warn', ...)`,
  never throws, never blocks the task-finish path.

**Owner:** Engineer (`runner.js`, ~15-20 line diff plus the new dir
bootstrap + `.gitignore` entry — same shape as the ledger commit almost
exactly, which makes this a fast, low-risk build). **Size:** small,
well-precedented.

### G3 — No single authoritative "base position" constant

**What exists:** two different, both-real, both-in-active-use values —
`overseer.mjs`'s `CAMP = {x:12, y:91, z:52}` (idle-guard/quarantine ring
math) and `CIV.md`'s prose "camp centered around (11-12, 89, 55-57)"
(human-facing description, roughly matching depot chest A's actual
position `(11,89,55)` which `panel.mjs`'s own `CHEST_META` already has
from Vault work).

**Ask — this one is a DECISION, not a code change, but it needs to be
made once and declared, or every future feature that says "distance from
base" silently disagrees with every other one.** Recommend: adopt chest
A's position, `(11, 89, 55)`, as the canonical `BASE_POS` — it's already
a real, physical, unambiguous landmark (not a "center of an imagined
ring"), it's already in `panel.mjs` today (Vault's `CHEST_META`), and it's
within a few blocks of both existing candidates so nothing currently
built on `overseer.mjs`'s `CAMP` breaks in practice if that stays
runner-side-only and panel.mjs declares its own `BASE_POS` for display
purposes (the two constants serve different consumers — one gates a
quarantine ring, one anchors a distance readout — they don't have to be
the literal same constant, but they SHOULD be within a few blocks of each
other and someone should say so out loud once).

**Owner:** team-lead/chief call on which literal point wins; whoever
decides, it's a one-line constant in `panel.mjs`, zero runner.js change
required — direction (compass bearing) is `atan2(dx, dz)` off `pos` vs.
`BASE_POS`, entirely client-or-server computable from data that already
exists.

hide only when "no data" is itself the normal/expected state (Vault's

### 3.1 Mission Control Cards

**This extends, not replaces, today's fleet-grid cards.** Rounds 1-5
already built idleGuard chip, lastDeath, 3-state connectivity dot, panic
flag, task-source chip, and the per-card event log onto the existing
card. v3 adds three new fields to the SAME card component plus a
drilldown, rather than introducing a parallel card system.

**Wall state (always visible, no click needed):**

| Field | Source | Empty/stale rule |
|---|---|---|
| current task kind + detail + state | `/status.currentTask` (existing) | unchanged — already handled |
| distance from base + direction | `/status.pos` vs. `BASE_POS` (G3) — `dist = sqrt(dx²+dz²)` (2D, matching how `overseer.mjs`'s own ring check ignores Y), `bearing` → 8-point compass (`N/NE/E/SE/S/SW/W/NW`) via `atan2` | `pos` null (offline/unspawned) → hide the whole badge, don't show "0m" |
| primary tool + durability bar | `/status.inventory`, filtered to the currently-equipped/most-relevant tool (pick the first tool-type item with a `durability` field — pickaxe/axe/sword priority order, matching what `ensureTool` already treats as "the" tool for a task) | G1 not shipped yet → hide the whole tool line, not a fake full bar; durability present but the item is a non-degrading tool variant (shouldn't happen post-G1, but if `max` is falsy, hide) |

the existing DONE-section/event-log expand language exactly):**

- Full inventory (today's card already shows top-10 chips; drilldown

### 3.2 Economy graphs

**Wall state:** a compact strip of small sparklines — one per tracked
item (`iron_ingot`, `wheat`, `bread` are chief's three named examples;
recommend generalizing to "top N items by ledger volume" rather than
hardcoding exactly three, so the wall stays useful as the tribe's economy
shifts) — each showing net flow over a fixed recent window (recommend
last 24h, hourly buckets — 24 data points is plenty for a glanceable
trend line and cheap to compute). Beside each sparkline, the current net
total for that window as a plain number (matches the "big number +
trend" pattern chief is already asking for on the stat wall, reused
here at item granularity).

**Drilldown (click a sparkline):** expand into a larger chart — longer
window (7 days, still hourly or daily-bucketed depending on volume),
per-bot breakdown of who contributed the flow (the ledger already tags
every entry with `bot`), and the raw parsed/unparsed entry list for that
item (mirrors `cave/ledger.mjs`'s own CLI output, just rendered instead
of printed).

**Harvest yields:** NOT a separate tracking mechanism — a wheat/bread
deposit IS a harvest yield, same ledger primitive, same aggregation.
Filtering the existing sparkline set to farm-relevant items (`wheat`,
`bread`, `wheat_seeds`) covers this without new code.

**Aggregation approach (server-side, `panel.mjs`):**

```js
// bucket ledger entries into hourly {ts, item} -> netDelta sums, over the
// requested window, per item. Read every cave/ledger/*.jsonl, filter
// unparsed entries out of the sums (same rule ledger.mjs already uses).
```

Cache on the NEWEST mtime across all ledger files (a directory scan,
`fs.readdir` + `Promise.all(fs.stat)`, take the max) — same discipline as
`/api/todo`/`/api/vault`, generalized to N files instead of one.

**Empty/stale states:** zero ledger files anywhere (fresh checkout, no
runner has deposited since the ledger primitive landed) → hide the whole
section, same rule as Vault's missing-snapshot case — "no economic
activity has ever been recorded" is a normal state for a brand-new
primitive, not a broken one. Once at least one file/entry exists, always
render (even a single data point is honest information, unlike an empty
audit which genuinely has nothing to say).

**Update cadence:** ledger files change only on deposit/withdraw events —
does NOT need the same 3s cadence as task status. Recommend a slower
cadence for this section specifically (e.g. 20-30s), decoupled from the
main `refresh()` loop's `Promise.all`, both because the data doesn't
change that fast and because re-scanning N ledger files 3x more often
than necessary is pure waste. This is the one section where I'd
recommend NOT reusing the exact same poll timer as everything else.

### 3.3 Tribe stat wall

Five big-number tiles, each independently sourced — a tile with no data
source should say so, not show a blank or a zero that could be
misread as "confirmed zero."

| Tile | Source | Formula | Empty/stale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deaths-free streak | `cave/deaths/<bot>.json` × 8 | days since the max `lastDeath.ts` across all files that exist; if NO file exists for any bot, render "no deaths recorded (since relaunch)" rather than a fake day-count | never hide this tile — "no deaths ever" is exactly the good-news state a stat wall exists to show |
| Total ore banked | Vault (`/api/vault`), summed across `ORE_ITEMS = ['iron_ingot','raw_iron','raw_copper','coal','copper_ingot']` (explicit allowlist — recommend NOT including `cobbled_deepslate`/`cobblestone`, which the tribe's own TODO.md vocabulary treats as building material, not banked wealth; team-lead can amend the list, but it should be a declared list, not implicit) | sum across all chests in the snapshot | Vault missing → hide this tile too (no ground truth exists) |
| Bread stock | Vault chest C `bread` count + summed `bread` across all 8 bots' `/status.inventory` (both candidates from §1.5 — recommend the sum since real tribe bread supply is genuinely both) | banked + carried | if Vault is missing, fall back to carried-only with a note ("carried only — no chest audit yet"), don't hide entirely since fleet data alone is still honest partial information |
| Missions today | G2 (`cave/missions/*.jsonl`), UTC-day filter, `counts !== false` | count | G2 not shipped → hide tile entirely (matches Mission Control's same rule — 0 would be ambiguous between "shipped, quiet day" and "not built yet") |
| FEL relation status | G4 (`cave/fel-relation.json`) | direct render of `status`+`note` | file missing → hide tile (matches Vault's rule exactly: "never recorded" is the honest normal state for a file nobody's written yet) |

**Drilldown per tile:** click "deaths-free streak" → full per-bot death
list (same data Mission Control's own drilldown uses, different entry
point); click "missions today" → per-bot mission breakdown; click "total
ore banked"/"bread stock" → the relevant Vault chest cards, scrolled/
highlighted; click "FEL relation" → the note + `updatedAt`/`updatedBy`,
maybe a short manually-maintained history if G4's file grows an array
form later (not needed for v1 of this tile — a single current-state
object is enough to start).

**Update cadence:** same 3s main cycle for deaths/ore/bread (data already
flowing through the main poll or cheap to add); missions and FEL status
can ride the slower economy-style cadence since neither changes
sub-minute.

---

## 4. ARCHITECTURE NOTE

### Current state

`cave/panel.mjs` is 1840 lines today (`cave/runner.js` is 2281, for
scale-of-comparison). Everything — HTTP routing, all data-layer parsing
(fleet aggregation, alerts, TODO board, Vault), the entire HTML document,
every rule of CSS, and the entire client-side JavaScript — lives in one
file, one giant template literal for the page. This has already cost one
real, twice-repeated bug this session: **a literal backslash inside a
client-side regex gets silently eaten by the OUTER template literal's own
escape processing**, because the served page's JS is textually nested
inside `panel.mjs`'s own JS as a string. I hit this exact class of bug in
round 5 (a regex) and caught a second, unrelated "wired but never called"
bug in round 7 only by grepping the SERVED output rather than trusting
the source. Both are symptoms of the same root cause: the client script
isn't really a separate program from the server's perspective, so nothing
(not `node --check`, not an editor, not a linter) can verify it as
JavaScript on its own — every check has to go through "extract the
`<script>` block from the rendered output first."

v3 adds three new sections, each with wall+drilldown state, at least one
new client-side rendering primitive (sparklines) that today's file has
never needed, and at minimum two new server-side data-layer modules
(ledger aggregation, mission-log reader) alongside the two that already
exist (TODO parser, Vault reader). Realistic estimate: v3 alone is
several hundred to ~1000 lines across CSS/HTML/JS. That would push
`panel.mjs` toward 2500-3000+ lines in one file — still technically fine
for Node to run, but past the point where "one file" is actually helping
anyone read, review, or safely hand pieces of it to parallel Workflow
agents without merge conflicts.

### Recommendation: split by CONCERN, not by adding a build step

"No build step" and "one file" are not the same constraint — Node ESM
already supports importing sibling `.mjs` files natively with zero
bundler, and a plain `<script src="/panel.js">` tag can point at a second
route this same `http.createServer` serves as a static file, still zero
build tooling, zero npm installs. Recommend three files, all still
plain, still zero-dependency, still no build step:

1. **`cave/panel.mjs`** stays the HTTP server + route table + the small
   amount of glue (cache objects, `handle()`). This is what boots, what
   `spawn.mjs`-equivalent tooling and the chief's restart routine already
   know about — its role/entry-point doesn't change.
2. **`cave/panel-data.mjs`** (new) — every server-side data-layer function
   that doesn't need `http`: `getTodoBoard`/`parseTodoMarkdown` (existing,
   move as-is), `getVault`/`buildVaultChests` (existing, move as-is), and
   the two new v3 readers (ledger aggregation, mission-log reader/G2
   consumer, deaths-streak scanner). Plain named exports, imported by
   `panel.mjs` with an ordinary `import { getVault, getTodoBoard, ... } from './panel-data.mjs'`.
   This is pure extraction of what's already cleanly self-contained in
   today's file (each of these functions already has zero dependency on
   `req`/`res` or the HTTP layer) — low-risk, mechanical, and immediately
   makes each parser independently testable (a Workflow agent can run
   `node -e "import('./panel-data.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.getVault()))"`
   without booting the whole server).
3. **`cave/panel-client.js`** (new) — the entire client-side script,
   moved out of the template literal into a real, standalone,
   directly-`node --check`-able JavaScript file, served via a new
   `GET /panel.js` route (`fs.readFile` + `content-type: application/javascript`,
   cached in memory the same way `renderPage()`'s HTML string could be)
   and referenced as `<script src="/panel.js"></script>` instead of an
   inline `<script>` block. This is the change that actually kills the
   double-escaping bug class at its root — a real `.js` file has no outer
   template literal to fight with, ever. It is also the single highest-
   leverage change for Workflow-safety: multiple implementation agents
   building Mission Control / Economy / Stat Wall in parallel will all be
   editing "the client script" simultaneously; today that means three
   agents fighting over one enormous template-literal string with
   escaping hazards baked in, versus three agents editing distinct
   well-defined regions of one real `.js` file with normal diff/merge
   semantics.

The HTML shell itself (the static skeleton — header, `<main>`, the
`#board`/`#vault` sections, footer) is small enough and changes rarely
enough that I'd leave it inline in `panel.mjs`'s `renderPage()` rather
than also extracting a template file — splitting three ways already gets
the real win; a fourth split (HTML) adds ceremony for little payoff at
this size.

### Sparklines: hand-rolled inline SVG, no library

Matches the file's zero-deps doctrine exactly and is genuinely simple at
this scale: a sparkline is `N` numbers mapped to an SVG `<path>`. One pure
function, testable in isolation, callable from `panel-client.js`:

```js
function sparklinePath(values, width, height) {
  if (!values.length) return '';
  var max = Math.max.apply(null, values), min = Math.min.apply(null, values);
  var range = max - min || 1;
  var stepX = width / Math.max(1, values.length - 1);
  return values.map(function (v, i) {
    var x = i * stepX;
    var y = height - ((v - min) / range) * height;
    return (i === 0 ? 'M' : 'L') + x.toFixed(1) + ',' + y.toFixed(1);
  }).join(' ');
}
```

Wall-state sparklines: no axes, no labels, no grid — just the path (plus
maybe a filled area under it for the "bank total" style tiles), matching
"dense, calm, no decorative noise." Drilldown charts can afford slightly
more (hour/day tick marks, a hover-value readout) but should still be
hand-rolled SVG, not a pulled-in charting library — the doctrine and the
data volume (dozens to low hundreds of points, not thousands) both argue
against needing one.

### Drilldown state

Client-side only, no server persistence needed — a plain per-card/
per-section `expanded` boolean, held in the same kind of module-level JS
object the DONE-section toggle and each card's `evState` already use
today. Re-rendered on the normal poll cycle; never a page reload; never
routed (no client-side router needed — this is explicitly NOT a
multi-page app, it's one page with inline reveal, matching everything
shipped so far). This is not a new pattern to invent, just the existing
one applied three more times.

### Refresh cadence

Recommend NOT putting every v3 fetch on the same single `Promise.all` at
the same 3s cadence. Task status (Mission Control's wall state) belongs
on the fast cycle — it's genuinely live. Economy graphs and the two
slow-moving Stat Wall tiles (missions today, FEL status) do not need
sub-30-second freshness and re-scanning ledger files that often is waste,
not diligence. Recommend a second, independent timer (e.g. 20s) for
economy + the slow stat tiles, decoupled from the main `refresh()`'s 3s
loop — both timers update the DOM in place exactly the same way, just at
different rates.

---

## Summary for the implementing Workflow

- **Buildable today, zero runner.js changes**: Economy graphs (ledger
  already exists), most of the Tribe Stat Wall (deaths-free streak, ore,
  bread — all already-available data), FEL relation tile IF G4's file is
  created by hand first (a `team-lead`/orchestrator action, not code).
- **Blocked on Engineer (parallel, independent asks)**: G1 (tool
  durability, ~10 lines), G2 (mission log, ~15-20 lines, precedented
  almost exactly by the ledger commit).
- **Blocked on a decision, not code**: G3 (which point is `BASE_POS`).
- **Architecture ask for whoever runs the implementation Workflow**: do
  the panel-data.mjs / panel-client.js split FIRST, before building v3's
  new sections into it — building three big new features into the
  current single-file-with-template-literal-JS shape guarantees more of
  the exact bug class this dossier already flagged twice.

const mcDataToNode = require('./lib/loader')
const cache = {} // prevent reindexing when requiring multiple time the same version

function getVersion (mcVersion) {
  if (cache[mcVersion]) { return cache[mcVersion] }
  const mcData = data[mcVersion]
  if (mcData == null) { return null }
  const nmcData = mcDataToNode(mcData, mcVersion)
  cache[mcVersion] = nmcData
  return nmcData
}

function toMajor (version) {
  const [a, b] = (version + '').split('.')
  return a + '.' + b
}

function minor (version) {
  const [, , c] = (version + '.0').split('.')
  return parseInt(c, 10)
}

module.exports = function (mcVersion) {
  // Check exact version first
  let assets = getVersion(mcVersion)
  if (assets) { return assets }
  // If not found, resort to the last of major
  assets = getVersion(lastOfMajor[toMajor(mcVersion)])
  return assets
}

input.new_string: base" needs ONE authoritative anchor, and today there isn't one. ### 1.10 `minecraft-assets` npm package — real item icons (CHIEF ADDITION, buy-before-build) **Already in `node_modules`, already a proven dependency in this exact tree — not a new install.** `node_modules/minecraft-assets` v1.19.0 (the NPM wrapper's own version number, unrelated to Minecraft's version), MIT-licensed wrapper by PrismarineJS, wrapping a data submodule at `node_modules/minecraft-assets/minecraft-assets/data//`. **Best of all, it's not a cold dependency** — `mineflayer-web-inventory` (already installed, used elsewhere in this project's mineflayer tooling) depends on `minecraft-assets` itself for exactly this job: rendering a web view of a bot's real inventory with real textures. This panel would be doing nothing this dependency tree hasn't already proven works. **Version match confirmed exact.** The cavecrew server runs Minecraft 1.21.11 (per `cave/BARITONE.md`'s fabric-mod version pins), and `minecraft-assets/minecraft-assets/data/1.21.11/` exists in this checkout right now — no version-gap fallback logic needed for the common case (the package's own `getVersion()` already has a last-of-major-version fallback built in for when it doesn't, worth using defensively anyway). **Layout, confirmed by directly inspecting the files:** ``` minecraft-assets/minecraft-assets/data/1.21.11/ items/*.png — 792 files, one per genuine item (tools, food, ingots — e.g. iron_pickaxe.png, bread.png, iron_ingot.png) blocks/*.png — 1210 files, one per block's inventory-icon texture (e.g. oak_log.png, cobblestone.png) — this is where BLOCK-type carried items live, since a block held in inventory shows its own block texture, not a separate "item" render items_textures.json / blocks_textures.json — index files (numeric-keyed arrays, not directly name-keyed — the flat filenames are the simpler and sufficient lookup for this use case) ``` Confirmed: filenames match `minecraft-data`'s own item/block names 1:1 (`iron_pickaxe.png`, `oak_log.png`) — **no name-mapping table is needed** for the common case. Total size for the matched version: ~20MB across ~2000 PNGs — small enough to serve on-demand with a simple in-memory cache (lazily populated per-name, not preloaded), never a real disk-space or memory concern at this item-name cardinality (the tribe's actual inventories/chests only ever touch a few dozen distinct item names, not all 2000). **Lookup rule** (two-tier, no external mapping needed): try `items/.png` first, fall back to `blocks/.png`, fall back to a generic "unknown item" placeholder icon (hand-drawn or a simple grey square — matches this file's "never show garbage, show an honest placeholder" doctrine) if neither exists — covers any exotic item name a future MC version or a typo introduces without ever 404-ing a chip's `` into a broken-image icon. **License note (asked for precisely, not glossed over):** the NPM wrapper's *code* is MIT. The *textures themselves* are Mojang's own copyrighted Minecraft assets, community-extracted and redistributed via this package — the wrapper's own README doesn't make an explicit redistribution-rights claim beyond linking to the upstream `rom1504/minecraft-assets` data repo, and neither does that repo. This is the same well-established (if legally informal) norm the entire mineflayer/PrismarineJS tooling ecosystem already operates on — this exact package is a direct, non-optional dependency of `mineflayer-web-inventory`, meaning it's already sitting in this project's own `node_modules` and already used by tooling this project already runs. Serving it is **local-only, never a CDN, never redistributed beyond `127.0.0.1`/the tailnet** (matches the panel's existing network posture exactly — see `PANEL.md`'s Host allow-list section) — the same "extracted from an asset pack a licensed client already has" posture every mineflayer bot on this server already relies on just to render blocks/items to itself. Flagging this precisely so the decision to ship it is made with eyes open, not because there's a real alternative that's meaningfully cleaner — there isn't one that gives *real* game textures, which is specifically what chief asked for ("actual game textures, not emoji/text"). ---

content.content: ### 1.10 `minecraft-assets` npm package — real item icons (CHIEF ADDITION, buy-before-build) **Already in `node_modules`, already a proven dependency in this exact tree — not a new install.** `node_modules/minecraft-assets` v1.19.0 (the NPM wrapper's own version number, unrelated to Minecraft's version), MIT-licensed wrapper by PrismarineJS, wrapping a data submodule at `node_modules/minecraft-assets/minecraft-assets/data//`. **Best of all, it's not a cold dependency** — `mineflayer-web-inventory` (already installed, used elsewhere in this project's mineflayer tooling) depends on `minecraft-assets` itself for exactly this job: rendering a web view of a bot's real inventory with real textures. This panel would be doing nothing this dependency tree hasn't already proven works. **Version match confirmed exact.** The cavecrew server runs Minecraft 1.21.11 (per `cave/BARITONE.md`'s fabric-mod version pins), and `minecraft-assets/minecraft-assets/data/1.21.11/` exists in this checkout right now — no version-gap fallback logic needed for the common case (the package's own `getVersion()` already has a last-of-major-version fallback built in for when it doesn't, worth using defensively anyway). **Layout, confirmed by directly inspecting the files:** ``` minecraft-assets/minecraft-assets/data/1.21.11/ items/*.png — 792 files, one per genuine item (tools, food, ingots — e.g. iron_pickaxe.png, bread.png, iron_ingot.png) blocks/*.png — 1210 files, one per block's inventory-icon texture (e.g. oak_log.png, cobblestone.png) — this is where BLOCK-type carried items live, since a block held in inventory shows its own block texture, not a separate "item" render items_textures.json / blocks_textures.json — index files (numeric-keyed arrays, not directly name-keyed — the flat filenames are the simpler and sufficient lookup for this use case) ``` Confirmed: filenames match `minecraft-data`'s own item/block names 1:1 (`iron_pickaxe.png`, `oak_log.png`) — **no name-mapping table is needed** for the common case. Total size for the matched version: ~20MB across ~2000 PNGs — small enough to serve on-demand with a simple in-memory cache (lazily populated per-name, not preloaded), never a real disk-space or memory concern at this item-name cardinality (the tribe's actual inventories/chests only ever touch a few dozen distinct item names, not all 2000). **Lookup rule** (two-tier, no external mapping needed): try `items/.png` first, fall back to `blocks/.png`, fall back to a generic "unknown item" placeholder icon (hand-drawn or a simple grey square — matches this file's "never show garbage, show an honest placeholder" doctrine) if neither exists — covers any exotic item name a future MC version or a typo introduces without ever 404-ing a chip's `` into a broken-image icon. **License note (asked for precisely, not glossed over):** the NPM wrapper's *code* is MIT. The *textures themselves* are Mojang's own copyrighted Minecraft assets, community-extracted and redistributed via this package — the wrapper's own README doesn't make an explicit redistribution-rights claim beyond linking to the upstream `rom1504/minecraft-assets` data repo, and neither does that repo. This is the same well-established (if legally informal) norm the entire mineflayer/PrismarineJS tooling ecosystem already operates on — this exact package is a direct, non-optional dependency of `mineflayer-web-inventory`, meaning it's already sitting in this project's own `node_modules` and already used by tooling this project already runs. Serving it is **local-only, never a CDN, never redistributed beyond `127.0.0.1`/the tailnet** (matches the panel's existing network posture exactly — see `PANEL.md`'s Host allow-list section) — the same "extracted from an asset pack a licensed client already has" posture every mineflayer bot on this server already relies on just to render blocks/items to itself. Flagging this precisely so

attachment.snippet:
1	# FLEET PANEL
2	
3	A read-mostly web dashboard for the cavecrew bot fleet. One page, eight cards,
4	live vitals, and exactly two buttons.
5	
6	The panel is a plain observer: it speaks the same public HTTP API a driver
7	speaks (`cave/DRIVER_GUIDE.md`) and knows nothing about runner internals. It
8	does not import `runner.js`, `skills.js`, or `overseer.mjs`, and it is not part
9	of the supervision loop — killing it affects nothing.
10	
11	## Files
12	
13	Three plain files, still zero-dependency, still no build step (PANEL V3 SPEC,
14	architecture note — split from one 1840-line file, phase 1, 2026-09-01):
15	
16	- **`cave/panel.mjs`** — the entry point. HTTP server, route table, the Host
17	  allow-list/CSRF guards, and the HTML shell (`renderPage()`: the static
18	  `<head>`/`<style>`/skeleton markup — small and rarely-changed enough to stay
19	  inline rather than earning a fourth file). This is what `node cave/panel.mjs`
20	  boots and what the chief's restart routine knows about; that doesn't change.
21	- **`cave/panel-data.mjs`** — every server-side data-layer function: fleet
22	  polling/aggregation, the alerts tail, the TODO board parser, the Vault
23	  reader, the two write actions (wake/stop), and the roster/chest tables they
24	  all share. Zero dependency on `req`/`res` — each function is independently
25	  testable without booting the HTTP server, e.g.
26	  `node -e "import('./cave/panel-data.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.getVault()))"`.
27	  Also carries the newer v3 primitives (`BASE_ANCHOR`, ledger/deaths/missions
28	  readers, the FEL relation reader). `BASE_ANCHOR`/`distanceFromBase()` and
29	  the per-bot mission reader are wired into Mission Control (see `## Mission
30	  Control drilldown` below); `getEconomy()` (built on the ledger reader) is
31	  wired into the `## Economy` section below. The deaths-streak and FEL
32	  relation readers remain unwired, waiting on the Tribe Stat Wall section —
33	  see `cave/PANEL_V3_SPEC.md` for what will consume them.
34	- **`cave/panel-client.js`** — the entire client-side script, served as a real
35	  static file via `GET /panel.js` and loaded with
36	  `<script src="/panel.js"></script>`. This is what used to be an inline
37	  template-literal `<script>` block inside `panel.mjs` — moving it out kills a
38	  bug class at the root: a literal backslash in a client-side regex had to be
39	  doubled to survive the outer template literal's own escape processing
40	  before the browser ever saw it (bit the file twice, rounds 5 and 7). As a
41	  real `.js` file there's no outer literal to fight, and `node --check` can
42	  verify it as JavaScript entirely on its own.
43	
44	## Start it
45	
46	```powershell
47	node cave/panel.mjs
48	```
49	
50	Then open <http://127.0.0.1:3200>.
51	
52	- **Panel port:** `3200`, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. Not reachable off the
53	  machine.
54	- **Runner ports polled:** `3201-3208` by default (the production fleet).
55	- **Dependencies:** none. Node built-ins only, no `npm install`.
56	
57	Stop it with Ctrl-C.
58	
59	### Port override
60	
61	`CAVE_PANEL_PORTS` replaces the default port list with a comma-separated one:
62	
63	```powershell
64	$env:CAVE_PANEL_PORTS = '3209'; node cave/panel.mjs
65	```
66	
67	This exists so the two write actions can be exercised against a throwaway test
68	runner without ever pointing at a production bot a driver owns. Point it at the
69	test port, click the buttons, confirm the behaviour, then restart without the
70	variable.
71	
72	`PANEL_PORT` (default `3200`) runs a second instance of the panel itself on a
73	different port — for developing the panel against the live, read-only fleet
74	without ever touching the production process on 3200:
75	
76	```powershell
77	$env:PANEL_PORT = '3290'; $env:CAVE_PANEL_PORTS = '3201,3202'; node cave/panel.mjs
78	```
79	
80	The Host allow-list is built off `PANEL_PORT`, so a dev instance allow-lists
81	its own port automatically. `3290` is the registered panel-dev port (see
82	`cave/CIV.md`'s port registry).
83	
84	A runner on a port outside the roster shows up under its `/status` name (or
85	`:PORT` if it is down), and its WAKE button falls back to the universally safe
86	`/collect {radius: 16}` sweep.
87	
88	## The two buttons
89	
90	These are the **only** write actions in the whole panel. There is no RCON, no
91	chat, no world manipulation, no `/eval`, and no other endpoint that mutates
92	anything.
93	
94	### WAKE — shown on idle cards only
95	
96	Pushes that bot's **role-default task**, mirrored from the `BOTS` list in
97	`cave/overseer.mjs` (~line 34). Each bot's first default is the one used, so a
98	click is deterministic:
99	
100	| Bot | Port | Wake pushes |
101	| --- | --- | --- |
102	| UngaBunga | 3201 | `/chop {count: 4, maxDistance: 48}` |
103	| Grog | 3202 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
104	| Zug | 3203 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
105	| Bonk | 3204 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
106	| Thak | 3205 | `/mine {block: 'coal_ore', count: 4, maxDistance: 28}` |
107	| Ook | 3206 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
108	| Durk | 3207 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
109	| Mog | 3208 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
110	
111	**Safety rule: `force: false`, always.** The flag is constructed inside
112	`doWake()` and is never read from the request body — there is no code path in
113	`panel.mjs` that can send `force: true`. So WAKE can never preempt a driver's
114	running task. If the runner is busy it answers `409` and the panel reports
115	`busy, not preempted` under the button, having changed nothing.
116	
117	The one thing WAKE does interrupt is the runner's own self-issued `idle-guard`
118	filler task, and that is the runner's behaviour, not the panel's: `startTask()`
119	in `runner.js` treats any real task as an automatic preemption of idle-guard,
120	with or without `force`. That is exactly what "wake an idle bot" means.
121	
122	WAKE also tags the push with `source: 'panel'`, so it shows up as itself in
123	the runner's own task/event log and the `/status` `currentTask.source` field
124	— previously indistinguishable from any other unidentified HTTP caller
125	(runner.js's own fallback is `'http'` when a caller doesn't self-identify).
126	The dashboard surfaces this as a small "via panel"/"via idle-guard" tag next
127	to the task's state pill, hidden for the plain `'http'` case since that is
128	today's common default for undated driver calls, not new information.
129	
130	A card counts as **idle** — amber border, WAKE button — when it has no current
131	task, its last task has already finished, or it is only running `idle-guard`.
132	
133	### STOP — shown on running non-idle tasks only
134	
135	Forwards `POST /stop` to that bot's runner, which cancels the current task
136	cleanly. Small and secondary on purpose: it is for calling off work you can see
137	going wrong, not for routine use. If a driver owns that bot, tell the driver.
138	
139	## What the page shows
140	
141	**Header** — `x/8 online`, `y idle`, and total `iron_ingot` across every
142	inventory against the 360 quota, with a progress bar. The dot on the right
143	blinks green on each successful poll.
144	
145	**Cards**, one per port, name tinted its Minecraft team colour:
146	
147	- connectivity dot, three states: green = bot connected, amber = runner
148	  process is up but the bot entity isn't (mid-reconnect), grey = runner
149	  unreachable
150	- rounded `xyz`, task age (best-effort)
151	- **distance from base** (v3, Mission Control) — one line under `xyz`:
152	  horizontal metres + an 8-point compass bearing (`N`/`NE`/`E`/`SE`/`S`/`SW`/
153	  `W`/`NW`) + vertical delta, all measured off `BASE_ANCHOR`
154	  (`panel-data.mjs`, currently chest A's real position, `11,89,55` — see G3
155	  in `cave/PANEL_V3_SPEC.md`). Horizontal distance is 2D (`x`/`z` only,
156	  matching how `overseer.mjs`'s own idle-guard ring check ignores `y`);
157	  vertical is a separate signed number so "how far sideways" and "how far
158	  up/down" stay two different readings, not one blended 3D figure. Hidden
159	  entirely — never a fabricated `0m` — whenever `pos` itself is unknown
160	  (offline/unspawned), and the compass point itself is omitted (not "N") the

## Start it

```powershell
node cave/panel.mjs
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:3200>.

- **Panel port:** `3200`, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. Not reachable off the

- **Runner ports polled:** `3201-3208` by default (the production fleet).
- **Dependencies:** none. Node built-ins only, no `npm install`.

Stop it with Ctrl-C.

`CAVE_PANEL_PORTS` replaces the default port list with a comma-separated one:

```powershell
$env:CAVE_PANEL_PORTS = '3209'; node cave/panel.mjs
```

This exists so the two write actions can be exercised against a throwaway test
runner without ever pointing at a production bot a driver owns. Point it at the
test port, click the buttons, confirm the behaviour, then restart without the
variable.

`PANEL_PORT` (default `3200`) runs a second instance of the panel itself on a
different port — for developing the panel against the live, read-only fleet
without ever touching the production process on 3200:

`cave/CIV.md`'s port registry).

`/collect {radius: 16}` sweep.

reserved baritone range) gets baritone-shaped parsing automatically, with or
without a named entry in `panel-data.mjs`'s `BOTS` table — adding a port here
is a config line, not a code change.

content.content:
1	# FLEET PANEL
2	
3	A read-mostly web dashboard for the cavecrew bot fleet. One page, eight cards,
4	live vitals, and exactly two buttons.
5	
6	The panel is a plain observer: it speaks the same public HTTP API a driver
7	speaks (`cave/DRIVER_GUIDE.md`) and knows nothing about runner internals. It
8	does not import `runner.js`, `skills.js`, or `overseer.mjs`, and it is not part
9	of the supervision loop — killing it affects nothing.
10	
11	## Files
12	
13	Three plain files, still zero-dependency, still no build step (PANEL V3 SPEC,
14	architecture note — split from one 1840-line file, phase 1, 2026-09-01):
15	
16	- **`cave/panel.mjs`** — the entry point. HTTP server, route table, the Host
17	  allow-list/CSRF guards, and the HTML shell (`renderPage()`: the static
18	  `<head>`/`<style>`/skeleton markup — small and rarely-changed enough to stay
19	  inline rather than earning a fourth file). This is what `node cave/panel.mjs`
20	  boots and what the chief's restart routine knows about; that doesn't change.
21	- **`cave/panel-data.mjs`** — every server-side data-layer function: fleet
22	  polling/aggregation, the alerts tail, the TODO board parser, the Vault
23	  reader, the two write actions (wake/stop), and the roster/chest tables they
24	  all share. Zero dependency on `req`/`res` — each function is independently
25	  testable without booting the HTTP server, e.g.
26	  `node -e "import('./cave/panel-data.mjs').then(m => console.log(m.getVault()))"`.
27	  Also carries the newer v3 primitives (`BASE_ANCHOR`/`RELAUNCH_TS`,
28	  ledger/deaths/missions readers, the FEL relation reader). `BASE_ANCHOR`/
29	  `distanceFromBase()` and the per-bot mission reader are wired into Mission
30	  Control (see `## Mission Control drilldown` below); `getEconomy()` (built
31	  on the ledger reader) is wired into the `## Economy` section below;
32	  `getDeathsStreak()`/`getMissionsToday()`/`readFelRelation()` plus Vault are
33	  composed by `getStatWall()` into the `## Tribe Stat Wall` section below.
34	- **`cave/panel-client.js`** — the entire client-side script, served as a real
35	  static file via `GET /panel.js` and loaded with
36	  `<script src="/panel.js"></script>`. This is what used to be an inline
37	  template-literal `<script>` block inside `panel.mjs` — moving it out kills a
38	  bug class at the root: a literal backslash in a client-side regex had to be
39	  doubled to survive the outer template literal's own escape processing
40	  before the browser ever saw it (bit the file twice, rounds 5 and 7). As a
41	  real `.js` file there's no outer literal to fight, and `node --check` can
42	  verify it as JavaScript entirely on its own.
43	
44	## Start it
45	
46	```powershell
47	node cave/panel.mjs
48	```
49	
50	Then open <http://127.0.0.1:3200>.
51	
52	- **Panel port:** `3200`, bound to `127.0.0.1` only. Not reachable off the
53	  machine.
54	- **Runner ports polled:** `3201-3208` (the mineflayer fleet) plus `3301` (the
55	  baritone fleet — see `## Baritone bots` below) by default.
56	- **Dependencies:** none. Node built-ins only, no `npm install`.
57	
58	Stop it with Ctrl-C.
59	
60	### Port override
61	
62	`CAVE_PANEL_PORTS` replaces the **entire** default port list (mineflayer +
63	baritone) with a comma-separated one:
64	
65	```powershell
66	$env:CAVE_PANEL_PORTS = '3209'; node cave/panel.mjs
67	```
68	
69	This exists so the two write actions can be exercised against a throwaway test
70	runner without ever pointing at a production bot a driver owns. Point it at the
71	test port, click the buttons, confirm the behaviour, then restart without the
72	variable.
73	
74	`CAVE_PANEL_BARITONE_PORTS` extends just the baritone side of the default list
75	without restating the whole mineflayer fleet — e.g. `3301,3302` once a second
76	baritone-controlled bot exists. Any port in `3301-3309` (`cave/CIV.md`'s
77	reserved baritone range) gets baritone-shaped parsing automatically, with or
78	without a named entry in `panel-data.mjs`'s `BOTS` table — adding a port here
79	is a config line, not a code change.
80	
81	`PANEL_PORT` (default `3200`) runs a second instance of the panel itself on a
82	different port — for developing the panel against the live, read-only fleet
83	without ever touching the production process on 3200:
84	
85	```powershell
86	$env:PANEL_PORT = '3290'; $env:CAVE_PANEL_PORTS = '3201,3202'; node cave/panel.mjs
87	```
88	
89	The Host allow-list is built off `PANEL_PORT`, so a dev instance allow-lists
90	its own port automatically. `3290` is the registered panel-dev port (see
91	`cave/CIV.md`'s port registry).
92	
93	A runner on a port outside the roster shows up under its `/status` name (or
94	`:PORT` if it is down), and its WAKE button falls back to the universally safe
95	`/collect {radius: 16}` sweep.
96	
97	## The two buttons
98	
99	These are the **only** write actions in the whole panel. There is no RCON, no
100	chat, no world manipulation, no `/eval`, and no other endpoint that mutates
101	anything.
102	
103	### WAKE — shown on idle cards only
104	
105	Pushes that bot's **role-default task**, mirrored from the `BOTS` list in
106	`cave/overseer.mjs` (~line 34). Each bot's first default is the one used, so a
107	click is deterministic:
108	
109	| Bot | Port | Wake pushes |
110	| --- | --- | --- |
111	| UngaBunga | 3201 | `/chop {count: 4, maxDistance: 48}` |
112	| Grog | 3202 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
113	| Zug | 3203 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
114	| Bonk | 3204 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
115	| Thak | 3205 | `/mine {block: 'coal_ore', count: 4, maxDistance: 28}` |
116	| Ook | 3206 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
117	| Durk | 3207 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
118	| Mog | 3208 | `/collect {radius: 16}` |
119	
120	**Safety rule: `force: false`, always.** The flag is constructed inside
121	`doWake()` and is never read from the request body — there is no code path in
122	`panel.mjs` that can send `force: true`. So WAKE can never preempt a driver's
123	running task. If the runner is busy it answers `409` and the panel reports
124	`busy, not preempted` under the button, having changed nothing.
125	
126	The one thing WAKE does interrupt is the runner's own self-issued `idle-guard`
127	filler task, and that is the runner's behaviour, not the panel's: `startTask()`
128	in `runner.js` treats any real task as an automatic preemption of idle-guard,
129	with or without `force`. That is exactly what "wake an idle bot" means.
130	
131	WAKE also tags the push with `source: 'panel'`, so it shows up as itself in
132	the runner's own task/event log and the `/status` `currentTask.source` field
133	— previously indistinguishable from any other unidentified HTTP caller
134	(runner.js's own fallback is `'http'` when a caller doesn't self-identify).
135	The dashboard surfaces this as a small "via panel"/"via idle-guard" tag next
136	to the task's state pill, hidden for the plain `'http'` case since that is
137	today's common default for undated driver calls, not new information.
138	
139	A card counts as **idle** — amber border, WAKE button — when it has no current
140	task, its last task has already finished, or it is only running `idle-guard`.
141	
142	### STOP — shown on running non-idle tasks only
143	
144	Forwards `POST /stop` to that bot's runner, which cancels the current task
145	cleanly. Small and secondary on purpose: it is for calling off work you can see
146	going wrong, not for routine use. If a driver owns that bot, tell the driver.
147	
148	## What the page shows
149	
150	**Header** — `x/8 online`, `y idle`, and total `iron_ingot` across every
151	inventory against the 360 quota, with a progress bar. The dot on the right
152	blinks green on each successful poll.
153	
154	**Cards**, one per port, name tinted its Minecraft team colour:
155	
156	- connectivity dot, three states: green = bot connected, amber = runner
157	  process is up but the bot entity isn't (mid-reconnect), grey = runner
158	  unreachable
159	- rounded `xyz`, task age (best-effort)
160	- **distance from base** (v3, Mission Control) — one line under `xyz`:
161	  horizontal metres + an 8-point compass bearing (`N`/`NE`/`E`/`SE`/`S`/`SW`/
162	  `W`/`NW`) + vertical delta, all measured off `BASE_ANCHOR`
163	  (`panel-data.mjs`, currently chest A's real position, `11,89,55` — see G3
164	  in `cave/PANEL_V3_SPEC.md`). Horizontal distance is 2D (`x`/`z` only,
165	  matching how `overseer.mjs`'s own idle-guard ring check ignores `y`);
166	  vertical is a separate signed number so "how far sideways" and "how far
167	  up/down" stay two different readings, not one blended 3D figure. Hidden
168	  entirely — never a fabricated `0m` — whenever `pos` itself is unknown
169	  (offline/unspawned), and the compass point itself is omitted (not "N") the
170	  rare time a bot is standing close enough to the anchor (under 1m) that a
171	  bearing would be noise, not information.
172	- movement deltas, `Δ30s 12.3 | Δ60s 25.1` (see below)
173	- health and food as 0-20 bars; health goes amber under 12, red under 6
174	- current task kind, state, and detail — when the task's `kind` is
175	  `panic-response` (the runner's own low-health flee/seal reflex taking over,
176	  see `runner.js`'s `triggerPanic`), the whole card and task box flag red,
177	  overriding the idle/err border colours. Rarest state a card can be in and
178	  the one most worth a glance across the room. Persists until the next task
179	  replaces `currentTask`, same STATUS-HOLD rule `lastError` already follows.
180	- `deathCount`, last death age (`(3m ago)`, hidden when there is none), the
181	  runner's `idleGuard` state (`guard on`/muted, `guard off`/amber — off is
182	  normal while a driver actively drives, see issue #6; older runners without
183	  the field just omit the chip), and movement engine
184	- `lastError` in a red box when set
185	- inventory as compact chips — top 10 stacks by count, with count badges.
186	  Any item carrying a real `durability: {used, max}` pair (a runner-side
187	  field, currently a live mix of present/absent even within the SAME bot's
188	  inventory depending on when each item was picked up relative to a runner
189	  restart — see G1 in `cave/PANEL_V3_SPEC.md`) grows a thin colour bar under
190	  its name+count: green at 30%+ remaining, amber 10-30%, red under 10% —
191	  vanilla Minecraft's own bottom-edge durability-bar convention, chief's
192	  exact thresholds from `cave/PANEL_V3_SPEC.md` §3.4. An item with no
193	  durability field renders byte-for-byte the same plain chip as before this
194	  round — zero fake bars, ever.
195	- a collapsed `▸ events (N)` toggle — click to expand the bot's last ~10
196	  events, newest first (see Phase 2 ideas below for detail)
197	- **Mission Control drilldown** (v3) — click anywhere on the card's header
198	  row (the dot/name/port/age line, marked `▸ details`) to reveal a panel with
199	  three sections, same max-height/opacity reveal language as the event log
200	  above (v3 deliberately does not invent a second expand motion):
201	  - **Full inventory** — every stack, not just today's top 10, same
202	    durability-bar chips as above, capped at 30 with a `+N more` chip past
203	    that (Vault's own precedent).
204	  - **Recent events** — the same ~10-event data as the compact toggle,
205	    fuller presentation; no new data source.
206	  - **Mission history** — up to the last 30 entries from
207	    `cave/missions/<bot>.jsonl` (G2), newest first, each showing kind, state,
208	    duration, and detail/error when present, fetched from `GET
209	    /api/missions?bot=<name-or-port>` **only while the drilldown is open** —
210	    deliberately not part of the fast 3s `/api/fleet` poll (see `## API`
211	    below). A bot with no mission file yet (G2 not shipped for it, or it has
212	    simply never finished a task) shows the honest quiet line `keine
213	    Missions-Historie (runner-update ausstehend)` rather than an empty list
214	    or a fabricated zero.
215	
216	Offline runners are tolerated, never fatal: the card dims, the entry is marked
217	`offline: true` with a reason, and the rest of the fleet renders normally.
218	
219	**Alerts column** — the tail of the overseer's escalation log merged with every
220	bot's live `lastError`, newest first.
221	
222	**Economy** (v3) — below the fleet grid, full width, above the Tribe Board:
223	one row per tracked item (`iron_ingot`, `raw_iron`, `wheat`, `bread`,
224	`oak_log`, `cobblestone` — a fixed, explicit allowlist, not "whatever moved
225	today") that has had any deposit/withdraw movement in the last 6 hours, each
226	row a hand-rolled inline SVG sparkline (36 ten-minute buckets, dots on the
227	buckets that actually moved, hover a dot for its exact signed value), the
228	window's net total, and a relative "last movement" time. An item on the
229	allowlist with zero movement in the window is simply omitted, never rendered
230	as a flat zero line. See `## Economy` below for the full contract.
231	
232	**Tribe board** — below the fleet grid, full width: `cave/TODO.md`'s work
233	state, parsed server-side into three groups — DOING and QUEUED always shown,
234	DONE collapsed behind a `▸ DONE (N)` toggle (same expand motion as a card's
235	event log). Each row is lane, task text, one chip per name in the `Who`
236	column (a chip tints to that bot's team colour when the name matches the
237	roster, plain otherwise — Krug/orchestrator/loose prose render as ordinary
238	chips, not guessed at), and whatever detail is left in `Status` once the
239	bucket's own keyword (doing/todo/done) is stripped off (`queued after #5`,
240	`blocked on cobble`, `law` all survive — they're real information the bucket
241	label alone doesn't carry). A malformed row (wrong cell count, no `Task`
242	cell) is counted and skipped rather than guessed at or thrown on; the count
243	shows in the board's subtitle when non-zero. See `## TODO board` below for
244	the parsing rules in full.
245	
246	**Vault** — below the tribe board, full width: `cave/audit-snapshot.json`'s
247	ground-truth depot ledger (written by `cave/audit.mjs`'s read-only chest
248	walk). One card per chest — label, coords, item chips in the same style as
249	a bot's own inventory, total item count — plus the whole snapshot's age up
250	top, amber past 2 hours. A chest `audit.mjs` failed to read (its `__error`
251	shape) renders as "read failed: `<message>`" instead of empty/garbage item
252	chips, with the chest's card border tinted amber. The section is hidden
253	outright — not shown empty — when the snapshot file has never been written;
254	"audit never ran yet" is a normal state, not a broken one. Any other read
255	failure (permissions, corrupt JSON) DOES show the section, with the failure
256	message where the age would be, since that IS worth noticing. See `## Vault`
257	below for the field-by-field detail.
258	
259	Auto-refresh is every 3s and updates the DOM in place — no page reload, no
260	flicker. Task ages tick locally each second between polls. The Economy
261	section (v3) is the one exception: it polls `/api/economy` on its own
262	independent ~20s timer rather than riding the main 3s loop — see `## Economy`
263	below for why.
264	
265	## Movement deltas
266	
267	Each card shows how far the bot actually got in the last 30 and 60 seconds:
268	
269	```
270	Δ30s 12.3 | Δ60s 25.1
271	```
272	
273	A delta is the straight-line 3D distance between the bot's current position and
274	its recorded position nearest N seconds ago — endpoint to endpoint, not path
275	length. That is deliberate: the question being answered is "did it get
276	anywhere", which is the wedge question, and it costs one square root.
277	
278	Colours, one decimal place:
279	
280	| Value | Colour | Means |
281	| --- | --- | --- |
282	| `> 5` | green | moving normally |
283	| `0.5` - `5` | amber | crawling, or working in place |
284	| `< 0.5` | red | **wedge flag** — pairs with the runner's own wedge watchdog |
285	| `—` | grey | no reading (see below) |
286	
287	A delta reads `—` when the bot is offline, has no position, or the ring has no
288	sample old enough to measure that window (within a 7.5s tolerance). Expect
289	dashes for the first 30-60 seconds after a panel restart — that is the honest
290	answer, not a bug.
291	
292	### Self-polling
293	
294	The panel polls the whole fleet **every 5 seconds on its own timer, whether or
295	not a browser is attached**, and appends each bot's position to an in-memory
296	ring about 65 seconds deep.
297	
298	This matters: if sampling were driven by the page, opening the tab would show
299	dashes for the first minute every time. Because the server samples on its own,
300	deltas are already warm when the page is opened, and they survive browser
301	refreshes. Request serving still goes through the normal 2s cache — the
302	self-poll only keeps that cache warm.
303	
304	The ring is in-memory only. It resets when the panel process restarts, and
305	there is no persistence by design.
306	
307	## API
308	
309	| Method | Path | Does |
310	| --- | --- | --- |
311	| `GET` | `/` | the dashboard, one self-contained HTML document |
312	| `GET` | `/api/fleet` | every runner's `/status` polled in parallel (3s timeout each), with the last ~10 `/events` merged per bot and `delta30`/`delta60` movement figures; whole aggregate cached 2s |
313	| `GET` | `/api/alerts` | last ~50 lines of the alerts log |
314	| `GET` | `/api/todo` | `cave/TODO.md`'s markdown tables, parsed and bucketed into `doing`/`todo`/`done`; cached on the file's mtime |
315	| `GET` | `/api/vault` | `cave/audit-snapshot.json`'s per-chest ledger, joined with hand-synced chest coords/labels; cached on the file's mtime, snapshot age always computed fresh |
316	| `GET` | `/api/economy` | (v3) per-item, time-bucketed net-flow series over `cave/ledger/*.jsonl` for a fixed six-item allowlist, last 6h in 10-min buckets; entries cached on the ledger directory's newest mtime, buckets recomputed fresh every call (the window is relative to "now"). Fetched by the client on its own ~20s timer, decoupled from the 3s fleet poll — see `## Economy` below. |
317	| `GET` | `/api/missions?bot=<name-or-port>` | one bot's mission history (v3, `cave/missions/<bot>.jsonl`), newest first, capped at 30 — see `## Mission Control drilldown` above. `bot` accepts the same name/port shapes as `wake`/`stop`. Fetched by the client only while that card's drilldown is open, not on the main poll. |
318	| `GET` | `/api/statwall` | (v3) the Tribe Stat Wall's five tiles in one payload — deaths-free streak, Vault-derived ore/bread totals, missions-today count, FEL relation status — see `## Tribe Stat Wall` below. Fetched by the client on the same ~20s timer as `/api/economy`. |
319	| `POST` | `/api/wake` | `{bot}` — push the role-default task, `force: false` |
320	| `POST` | `/api/stop` | `{bot}` — forward `POST /stop` |
321	
322	Everything else 404s.
323	
324	`bot` accepts a name (`"Thak"`, case-insensitive) or a port (`3205`, `":3205"`),
325	and must be on the panel's current port list. The page itself always sends the
326	port, since that is the one identifier a card can never have wrong.
327	
328	### Request guards
329	
330	Binding to `127.0.0.1` keeps other machines out, but it does not keep out a web
331	page the operator happens to have open — browsers will issue cross-origin
332	requests at localhost. Two guards close that, and both are needed:
333	
334	- **Host allow-list, all requests.** Anything whose `Host` header is not
335	  `127.0.0.1:3200`, `localhost:3200` or `[::1]:3200` gets `403`. This is the
336	  DNS-rebinding guard: a hostile page can point a domain it controls at
337	  `127.0.0.1`, but the request still arrives carrying that attacker hostname.
338	- **`application/json` required on writes.** `text/plain`, form-urlencoded and
339	  multipart are CORS-*simple* content types — a page can POST them
340	  cross-origin with no preflight at all, and `mode: 'no-cors'` hides the
341	  response while the mutation still lands. Anything else gets `415`, checked
342	  before the body is read and long before anything is forwarded to a runner, so
343	  a rejected request never touches a bot. Requiring JSON forces a preflight,
344	  and since the panel sends no CORS headers that preflight fails.
345	
346	Notes on the aggregate:
347	
348	- A slow or dead runner is caught per-bot; one bad runner can never fail the
349	  whole `/api/fleet` response.
350	- Concurrent refreshes collapse onto a single poll, so a hammered dashboard
351	  does not multiply into N parallel pokes at every runner.
352	- Events are pulled incrementally with `?since=<seq>` rather than re-fetching
353	  the full 500-entry ring every tick. A runner restart resets its seq, which the
354	  panel detects and re-syncs from 0.
355	- The alerts log is read from `cave/logs/alerts.log`, with `cave/alerts.log`
356	  checked as a fallback. A missing file is normal — it just means nothing has
357	  ever escalated — and returns an empty list, not an error.
358	
359	## TODO board
360	
361	`/api/todo` reads `cave/TODO.md` and re-parses it only when the file's mtime
362	changes — a stat() on every request, a re-read+re-parse only on an actual
363	edit. Parsing is by markdown table, not by line position, so it survives the
364	file being hand-edited:
365	
366	- A table is recognized by its header row being immediately followed by a
367	  GFM separator row (`|---|---|...`). Column names are matched
368	  case-insensitively against known aliases (`Lane`, `Task`, `Who`/`By`,
369	  `Status`) — a table with no recognizable `Task` column is skipped
370	  entirely (not guessed at), so an unrelated table elsewhere in the file
371	  (there is none today, but nothing stops one being added) can't get pulled
372	  in by accident.
373	- A body row whose cell count doesn't match its header's, or whose `Task`
374	  cell is empty, is counted and skipped rather than shifted into the wrong
375	  column or thrown on. The count surfaces in the page's board subtitle
376	  (`cave/TODO.md — 2 rows skipped (malformed)`) when it's non-zero, silent
377	  otherwise.
378	- A table with no `Status` column (the `## DONE` section: `Task`, `By`) has
379	  every row in it default to `done` — keyed off the table sitting directly
380	  under a heading matching `/^done/i`, not guessed from row content.
381	- Each row's `Status` text is bucketed by its own leading word: `doing`,
382	  `done`, or anything else (`todo`, `queued`, `queued after #5`, `blocked on
383	  cobble`, `law`, ...) falls into `todo`. The bucket's own keyword is then
384	  stripped from the text shown in the UI (redundant once a row is already
385	  grouped under "DOING"/"QUEUED"/"DONE") — everything after it survives,
386	  since that's real information the bucket label alone doesn't carry.
387	- Each `Who` token (split on `,`/`+`) is resolved against the roster
388	  (`BOT_BY_NAME`, the same table the fleet cards use) for a team colour; an
389	  unrecognized token (a driver name, "orchestrator", loose prose) still
390	  renders as a chip, just uncoloured — the parser never tries to guess
391	  which words in freeform prose are "really" a bot name.
392	
393	## Economy
394	
395	`/api/economy` reads every `cave/ledger/<bot>.jsonl` (written by `runner.js`'s
396	`appendLedgerLine()`, the single choke point every `DEPOT`-prefixed status
397	line passes through — see `cave/ledger.mjs`'s own header for the format) and
398	buckets each tracked item's parsed deltas into a 6-hour sliding window, ten
399	minutes per bucket (36 buckets total).
400	
401	- **Tracked items** — a fixed, explicit allowlist:
402	  `iron_ingot`, `raw_iron`, `wheat`, `bread`, `oak_log`, `cobblestone`
403	  (`ECONOMY_KEY_ITEMS`, `panel-data.mjs`). Deliberately not "top N by ledger
404	  volume" — a row set that means the same thing every time it renders beats
405	  one that reshuffles as the tribe's economy shifts. An allowlisted item with
406	  zero movement in the window is omitted entirely, never rendered as a flat
407	  zero line — the same "never fabricate" rule as everywhere else on this
408	  page.
409	- **Parsed vs. unparsed** — mirrors `cave/ledger.mjs`'s own rule exactly: a
410	  line only counts toward a bucket's sum when it has a clean numeric `delta`
411	  (`typeof delta === 'number'`); a correction/malformed `DEPOT`-ish line
412	  (`raw` + `parsed:false`) is read but never summed.
413	- **Caching** — two layers, the same split Vault's age-vs-snapshot uses: the
414	  parsed ledger entries are cached on the ledger directory's newest file
415	  mtime (generalizing the single-file mtime check `/api/todo`/`/api/vault`
416	  already use to N files), re-read only when a bot actually
417	  deposits/withdraws. The time-bucketed series itself is recomputed fresh on
418	  every single call, cache hit or not — the 6h window is relative to "now",
419	  which moves every second, so baking bucket boundaries into the mtime-keyed
420	  cache would freeze the window at whatever "now" was when the ledger last
421	  changed.
422	- **Update cadence** — the client fetches `/api/economy` on its own ~20s
423	  timer, decoupled from the main 3s `refresh()` loop: ledger files only
424	  change on a deposit/withdraw event, not sub-second like task status, so
425	  polling them at the fast cadence would be pure waste.
426	- **Empty/missing states** — three, each distinct and honest:
427	  - No `cave/ledger/` directory, or a directory with zero `.jsonl` files:
428	    `{ok:true, missing:true}`, and the whole section hides via `hidden`
429	    (same rule as Vault's missing-snapshot case) — "no economic activity has
430	    ever been recorded" is a normal state for a brand-new primitive, not a
431	    broken one.
432	  - Ledger file(s) exist but nothing in them has a clean numeric `delta`
433	    (only unparsed correction lines so far, or a freshly-created empty
434	    file): `{ok:true, missing:false, empty:true, items:[]}` — the section
435	    shows, with the line `Ledger leer — Bewegungen erscheinen ab jetzt`.
436	  - Real parsed movement exists somewhere in the ledger, just not for any
437	    allowlisted item within the 6h window: `{ok:true, missing:false,
438	    empty:false, items:[]}` — a different honest fact from "leer" above (the
439	    ledger isn't empty, the tracked items just haven't moved), so the client
440	    shows its own distinct line, `keine Bewegung bei erfassten Items (letzte
441	    6h)`, rather than reusing the "leer" message.
442	- **Rendering** — one row per active item: a hand-rolled inline SVG
443	  sparkline (no library, vanilla `<path>`/`<circle>`/`<line>` built via
444	  `document.createElementNS`, matching the whole page's zero-deps doctrine),
445	  a zero baseline, a line through all 36 buckets, and a dot only on buckets
446	  that actually moved (36 mostly-zero buckets would otherwise drown a real
447	  1-4-datapoint window in near-invisible zero-baseline markers) — hovering a
448	  dot shows its exact signed value via `<title>`. Beside the sparkline: the
449	  window's net total (green when positive, red when negative, muted at
450	  exactly zero) and a relative "last movement" time that ticks every second
451	  like every other clock on this page. Item name/sparkline colour comes from
452	  a fixed `--econ-*` token per item (`panel.mjs`'s `:root` block) — a
453	  deliberately different hue family from the red/amber/green severity set
454	  (that trio means "something's wrong" everywhere else on the page) and from
455	  `TEAM_HEX` (that set means "which bot", a different identity axis).
456	
457	## Vault
458	
459	`/api/vault` reads `cave/audit-snapshot.json` — the file `cave/audit.mjs`
460	writes after walking every registered chest with a live bot and reading its
461	real contents over HTTP (`/goto` + `/eval` openChest, read-only end to end).
462	Same mtime-cache shape as `/api/todo`, with one deliberate difference: the
463	snapshot's **age** is never part of the cached value. The whole point of
464	caching on mtime is that the file can sit unchanged — and therefore
465	increasingly stale — for a long time between audit runs while this endpoint
466	keeps getting polled every 3s; baking a relative age into the cached object
467	would freeze it at whatever it was when the cache was last built. Age is
468	computed fresh from the raw timestamp on every single call instead, cache
469	hit or not, so "2h 15m ago" always means what it says.
470	
471	- A chest ID (e.g. `chest_a_materials`) is joined against `CHEST_META`, a
472	  hand-synced copy of `audit.mjs`'s own `CHESTS` list (coords + label) —
473	  `audit.mjs` is a one-shot CLI script with no module exports, so this can't
474	  be imported, same contract as the `BOTS`/`TEAM_HEX` tables. Keep it in
475	  sync when a chest moves, or gets added/removed from BASE.md's registry.
476	- A chest whose value is the `{ __error: "<message>" }` shape (audit.mjs's
477	  own failure marker for a chest it couldn't reach or read) renders as "read
478	  failed: `<message>`" with an amber-tinted card border — amber, not red:
479	  a failed *read* is a data-collection problem worth a glance, not
480	  necessarily a fleet emergency the way a panic-response task is.
481	- Snapshot age past `VAULT_STALE_MS` (2 hours) tints amber in the section
482	  header. The threshold ships from the server (`staleMs` in the response),
483	  not hardcoded twice.
484	- Missing file (`ENOENT` — `audit.mjs` has simply never been run) returns
485	  `{ ok: true, missing: true }` and the whole section hides via the `hidden`
486	  attribute, not an empty-state message — this is the one case in the whole
487	  panel where "nothing to show" means "hide the section" rather than "show
488	  it saying so", because unlike an empty inventory or a quiet alerts log,
489	  "never audited" isn't really a state of the *fleet* at all. Any OTHER
490	  failure (permissions, corrupt JSON) still shows the section, with the
491	  failure message where the age normally goes, since that IS a problem
492	  worth surfacing.
493	- Item chips reuse the exact same `.chip` markup/style a bot card's own
494	  inventory uses — deliberately: a chest's contents and a bot's inventory
495	  are the same kind of fact, so they read the same way. Capped at 30 per
496	  chest with a "+N more" trailing chip past that (not needed by today's
497	  real chests — chest A currently sits at 23 distinct stacks — but a static
498	  page shouldn't quietly render an unbounded chip wall if that ever grows).
499	
500	## Tribe Stat Wall
501	
502	Five glance-readable big-number tiles, `#statwall`, sitting between the
503	sticky header and the fleet grid — the very first thing under the header per
504	the launch brief's layout ask. `/api/statwall` composes all five from disk
505	reads only (no runner poll): `getDeathsStreak()`, `getVault()`'s chest totals
506	under two allowlists, `getMissionsToday()`, and `readFelRelation()`
507	(`panel-data.mjs`). Rides the same ~20s client timer as `/api/economy` — none
508	of the five sources changes sub-minute (a death/mission file only gets
509	written on a death/task-finish event, Vault only on an audit run,
510	`fel-relation.json` only by hand), so a third poll tier would be waste, not
511	diligence.
512	
513	Four of the five tiles hide outright (`hidden`) when their one honest source
514	has never produced anything — same "no ground truth, no tile" rule Vault's
515	own section already follows, never a fabricated zero standing in for "not
516	built yet." The deaths tile is the one exception: it never hides, since
517	"no deaths ever" is exactly the good-news state this wall exists to show.
518	
519	- **Ohne Tod** (`sw-deaths`) — days (or hours, under 1 day) since the most
520	  recent `lastDeath.ts` across every `cave/deaths/<bot>.json` that exists
521	  (`getDeathsStreak()`). No death files at all — today's real state — reports
522	  `everDied:false` and anchors the count to `RELAUNCH_TS`
523	  (`panel-data.mjs`, hand-declared and sourced from `REBUILD.md`'s own R1
524	  section, same "declare it once" treatment `BASE_ANCHOR` gets), rendering
525	  "0 Tode seit Relaunch (dd.mm.yyyy)". A real death instead renders "letzter
526	  Tod (`<bot>`)". The number+unit re-derives every second off the same
527	  `sinceTs` field (the shared 1s age-ticker interval also drives this tile),
528	  same "every relative clock on this page keeps counting between polls"
529	  rule `taskAge`/`refreshTimestamps` already follow.
530	- **Erz gebankt** (`sw-ore`) — `iron_ingot` + `raw_iron` + `raw_copper` +
531	  `coal` summed across every readable Vault chest (`ORE_ITEMS`,
532	  `panel-data.mjs` — deliberately narrower than `PANEL_V3_SPEC.md` §3.3's
533	  optional 5-item suggestion, drops `copper_ingot`). A chest with a read
534	  error (`__error`-shaped) is excluded from the sum, not guessed at.
535	- **Brot-Vorrat** (`sw-bread`) — Vault's `bread` count only. Deliberately
536	  narrower than `PANEL_V3_SPEC.md` §3.3's "banked + carried" full
537	  recommendation (which would also sum every bot's live
538	  `/status.inventory`) — the launch brief asked for the audit-snapshot
539	  number specifically, so unlike the fuller spec this tile hides on a
540	  missing Vault rather than falling back to a carried-only partial figure.
541	- Both Vault-sourced tiles share one `vaultTile()` helper
542	  (`panel-data.mjs`) and Vault's own three states: missing snapshot → tile
543	  hidden; snapshot exists but fails to read/parse → tile shows, with the
544	  error text where the total normally goes; snapshot reads clean → total +
545	  Vault's own freshly-computed `ageMs`/`staleMs`, tinting the tile's left
546	  border amber past the same 2h staleness threshold `#vault`'s own age line
547	  uses.
548	- **Missionen heute** (`sw-missions`) — count of `cave/missions/*.jsonl`
549	  lines with `counts !== false` whose `ts` falls in the current UTC
550	  calendar day, across all bots (`getMissionsToday()`). Zero mission files
551	  anywhere hides the tile — a rendered `0` would otherwise be ambiguous
552	  between "shipped, quiet day so far" and "not built yet", the same
553	  ambiguity Mission Control's own per-card mission line already avoids.
554	- **FEL-Status** (`sw-fel`) — a direct render of `cave/fel-relation.json`'s
555	  `status` + `headline` (G4; hand-maintained, updated by the orchestrator
556	  when something relation-worthy happens). Missing file hides the tile
557	  (matches Vault's own missing-snapshot rule exactly). `status` drives the
558	  tile's accent colour via a `fel-<status>` CSS class against the five-state
559	  enum (`allied`/`trading`/`neutral`/`tense`/`disputed`) — `allied` reuses
560	  `--green` verbatim (chief's own instruction: the same "good" green a
561	  driver already reads off a card's connected-dot); the other four get their
562	  own `--fel-*` tokens (`panel.mjs` `:root`). An unrecognised status string
563	  still renders in plain text with the default border — no CSS class match
564	  is a cosmetic miss, never a broken tile.
565	
566	## Keeping it in sync
567	
568	`cave/panel-data.mjs` carries its own copy of three tables, because none of
569	their sources can be imported (`overseer.mjs` starts its supervision loop on
570	import; `runner.js` is a per-bot process; `audit.mjs` is a one-shot CLI
571	script that calls `main()` directly with no module exports):
572	
573	- the roster + role-default tasks, from `overseer.mjs`'s `BOTS` (~line 34)
574	- the team colours, from `runner.js`'s `TEAM_COLORS` (~line 78), lifted to hex
575	  values that stay readable on a dark card (`blue` and `dark_aqua` are
576	  brightened off their literal chat colours; the rest are palette values)
577	- the chest coords + labels, from `audit.mjs`'s `CHESTS` (~line 36), as
578	  `CHEST_META`
579	
580	If any of these change upstream, update `panel-data.mjs` by hand.
581	
582	## Phase 2 ideas
583	
584	Not built unless marked DONE below.
585	
586	- **Event feed** — DONE. Each card carries a collapsed-by-default `▸ events
587	  (N)` toggle in its footer row; expanding it shows the bot's last ~10 events
588	  (task starts/stops, idle-guard toggles, deaths, panics, chat, connect/
589	  disconnect — whatever `runner.js` pushes), newest first, in a small
590	  scrollable list. Deliberately per-card rather than a merged fleet-wide
591	  stream: a merged feed would compete with the Alerts column for the same
592	  "something's wrong" job, where this answers "what has this bot actually
593	  been doing lately." Relative timestamps refresh every poll even when the
594	  list itself hasn't changed (same honesty-over-shortcuts rule the movement
595	  deltas and task age already follow); the list only rebuilds its DOM when
596	  the underlying event set actually changes, so an open/scrolled log doesn't
597	  jump on an empty poll. Timestamps render in the card's monospace stack
598	  (ledger, not prose). Expand/collapse animates via max-height/opacity
599	  instead of snapping, and `#grid` sets `align-items: start` so a card that
600	  grows no longer stretches its same-row neighbours' backgrounds into dead
601	  space — a static grid still reflows rows below it, which isn't the "jump"
602	  a measured-height overlay would be needed to fully avoid. `runner.js`'s
603	  rate-cap rollup lines (`...suppressed N similar <type> event(s)`, RING
604	  RATE CAP fix) render italicized to read as a footnote about the log
605	  itself rather than a real event, detected by message shape since the
606	  rollup keeps its original event type.
607	- **Driver states** — show which bot has a driver attached and what that driver
608	  currently believes it is doing, so the panel distinguishes "idle" from
609	  "between driver steps".
610	- **TODO board view** — DONE. A full-width "Tribe Board" section below the
611	  fleet grid rather than a column beside it (the aside column is already
612	  claimed by Alerts) — DOING/QUEUED always shown, DONE collapsed. See
613	  `## TODO board` above for the parsing rules.
614	- **Scoreboard integration** — pull `cave/scoreboard-state.json` for quota
615	  progress, per-bot contribution, and trend over time rather than a single iron
616	  count.
617	- **Discord feed** — mirror the alerts column into the channel `discord.mjs`
618	  already talks to, and surface recent Discord chatter on the page.
